classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught sector-perimeter formula to semicircles, quadrants and a three-quarter circle, distinguishing radius from diameter.

content.prompt: Calculate the perimeter of these shapes. Answer to 1 d.p.

spec.description: Upper semicircle with a horizontal diameter and a double-ended measurement arrow spanning the entire base.
spec.mathematics: The diameter is 4 cm, so the radius is 2 cm; the arc subtends 180 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given diameter is visible.

spec.description: Upper semicircle with a measurement arrow extending from the left endpoint to the midpoint of the horizontal base.
spec.mathematics: The measured half-diameter is the radius, 4 cm; the arc subtends 180 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given radius is visible.

spec.description: Upper semicircle with a measurement arrow extending from the left endpoint to the midpoint of the horizontal base.
spec.mathematics: The radius is 2 cm; the arc subtends 180 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given radius is visible.

spec.description: Quarter circle centred at the lower-left corner, bounded by perpendicular vertical and horizontal radii. The measurement arrow spans the horizontal radius.
spec.mathematics: The radius is 2 cm; the arc subtends 90 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given radius is visible.

spec.description: Quarter circle centred at the lower-left corner, bounded by perpendicular vertical and horizontal radii. The measurement arrow spans the horizontal radius.
spec.mathematics: The radius is 0.2 cm; the arc subtends 90 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given radius is visible.

spec.description: Three-quarter circle with the lower-right quadrant removed. Its straight boundary consists of rightward and downward radii; the measurement arrow spans the rightward radius.
spec.mathematics: The radius is 0.2 cm; the major boundary arc subtends 270 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given radius is visible.
